policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 7:2 reads 'upon the four corners of the land'. The qere absolute ארבע and the ketiv construct ארבעת are both rendered by English 'the four corners' — the distinction is one of Hebrew bound form, which English number-plus-noun cannot show, and there is no ASV note mapped to this unit. Nothing in the wording excludes either reading; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 7:21 reads 'and they shall profane it', a plural subject taken up from 'the strangers' and 'the wicked of the earth'. The qere וְחִלְּלֽוּהוּ carries the plural ו before the object suffix; the ketiv consonants וחללה lack it and support only a singular verb with suffix. The plural English verb is the qere reading.
